Build the existing release benchmark before any core edit, copy its executable and all core/benchmark source inputs to a local archive, and record Rust version, flags, lockfiles, feature settings and licenses.

Run a baseline smoke invocation for each existing executable workload and a fresh historical-format run; bind the archive to the observed outputs and keep large artifacts out of Git.

tasks.title: Prepare bounded parallel register edge moves
tasks.input_output_contract: A bounded planner accepts typed source/destination slot moves and returns an immutable deterministic schedule that has the same result as simultaneous assignment. Numeric types describe values at the original source boundary: reads of one original source slot must agree on type, but target slots may be reused with another numeric type after the edge. It rejects out-of-range original slots, duplicate destinations, conflicting types for reads of the same original source slot, and work or byte budget excess before publication. It removes self-moves, schedules acyclic moves without overwriting a still-needed source, and breaks cycles with a symbolic Scratch value whose Save step records the NumericType. Save occurs before scratch-dependent reads; the one scratch value is reused across disconnected cycles, including mixed-type cycles. All four numeric types fit the safe u64 value representation; no scratch slot index is synthesized. Failure publishes no partial plan. The planner and its private unit tests compile only with register-executor, remain safe Rust, and do not expose a public planner API or select register execution.
implementation_steps: Define private checked move-request and immutable move-plan types using bounded slot indices and source-boundary NumericType values; validate original source/destination slot bounds, unique destinations, and consistent numeric types for reads of each original source slot before producing output. Permit destination slot type reuse across the edge.

Remove identity moves and construct a deterministic schedule for acyclic components, selecting only moves whose destination is no longer needed as a source; preserve simultaneous-assignment semantics for arbitrary input order.

Detect cycles and break each with one symbolic Scratch value; emit Save with the saved NumericType before scratch-dependent reads, then reuse that scratch value across disconnected cycles including mixed-type cycles. All four numeric types fit the safe u64 value representation, so do not synthesize a scratch slot index or reject a scratch type; account schedule steps and encoded bytes against shared work/byte limits with checked arithmetic.
Reserve and validate the complete bounded output before allocating/publishing it; every limit or arithmetic failure returns a decline without an observable partial plan.

Add the four private named planner unit cases and compare bounded generated schedules with a test-only simultaneous-assignment oracle; add a separate public integration policy guard proving register execution remains unavailable when the feature is disabled.

tasks.title: Integrate opt-in lazy Register entry
tasks.input_output_contract:
Add an opt-in Engine constructor such as `Engine::with_register_entry_threshold(config, threshold)` that selects the existing `ExecutionPolicy::Register` and stores a validated positive threshold privately. The existing `Engine::new` and `Engine::with_execution_policy(config, ExecutionPolicy::Register)` remain eager and behave exactly as before. The default policy remains Decoded.

For the opt-in constructor, `Engine::compile` stores a P133 lazy cache in the ModuleData owned by that module and does not create the eager whole-module `PreparedModule`. The cache remains shared through cloned `Module` values and across Stores using that Module; it does not retain `Arc<ModuleData>`. Keep the P133 engine/source owner check on lookup and publish.

At each new function entry, `Store::frame` performs one cache lookup for the function body. Before the hot threshold, a cold body starts decoded with no Register activation. At threshold, a completed cached function may initialize a Register `Activation` at PC 0. The `Activation` owns one `Arc<CachedFunction>` pin; `register::step` borrows the pinned function and never clones an `Arc` per opcode. Calls construct a new frame and count as new entries. A running frame is never promoted later, and continuation restoration never replays entry lookup, compiles, or restarts the frame.

When a Register prefix reaches its decoded handoff, it materializes once and drops the `Activation`, which releases its cache pin unless another live activation reference exists. An activation that is cloned or moved while still live naturally retains its own `Arc` pin across cache eviction. The P065 suspend/capture barrier first performs the decoded handoff, so the actual captured frame contains saved decoded state and no active Register pin; resumption continues that state without entry lookup, recompilation, or reactivation. Cache preparation itself does not charge guest fuel, check cancellation at a different source boundary, execute host code, repeat a side effect, mutate guest state, or alter trap and result behavior. No per-Store cache or duplicate compilation is introduced.

In `Engine::compile`, create/store a threshold-configured P133 cache for the opt-in path and skip eager `PreparedModule::prepare` only for that constructor. Store the cache on `ModuleData`, shared by all Module/Store clones and bound to the existing engine ID and source Arc. Keep eager preparation for the current Register constructor.

At `Store::frame`, make one cache lookup per body entry. On a ready result, create the existing activation from the cached `PreparedFunction` at PC 0 and move the returned `Arc<CachedFunction>` into that `Activation`. Keep activation and source values frame-local; `register::step` borrows the pinned function without cloning an Arc per opcode. If the lookup declines, use the unchanged decoded path for the whole frame.

Preserve activation-owned pinning through normal Register execution. At P064 decoded handoff, materialize once and drop the `Activation`; do not keep an obsolete pin on the decoded frame. If a live activation is cloned or moved into a captured segment, its Arc keeps the P133 metadata charged through eviction. For the actual P065 suspend/capture barrier, verify that handoff drops the activation before capture and that restoration continues decoded state without a new entry count, preparation attempt, OSR, or replay.

Add the current-only command:

```text

```

Accept `CALLS` only from **1, 10, 100, 10000**. The execution mode is exactly `register`. `eager` requires threshold `0` and uses the existing eager Register Engine constructor; `adaptive` requires a positive threshold and uses the P134 opt-in constructor. tasks.title: Analyze paired Register entry totals and phases
tasks.input_output_contract:
Expose:

```python
analyze(report: dict, collection_root: Path, allow_smoke: bool = False) -> dict
```

Require the P136 report to pass `entry_batch_compare.validate_report` against its collection root, including all untouched raw side records, report identity digest, pair joins, settings, fixtures, executables, and source/build records. Recheck referenced build records, executable hashes, fixture hashes, helper identities, and report/identity hashes before and after analysis. The producer and CLI also run P136's full source-current `verify_collection` wrapper against the recorded archive, adapter, candidate and harness inputs; never launch either executable or guest during analysis.

Production analysis requires `timing_evidence:true`, distinct archived/current source identities, exactly two independent runs with distinct seeds, the complete declared row matrix, and at least 30 complete pairs for every row in each run. Reject same-source aliases and smoke collections as production evidence. Reject missing, duplicate, foreign, stale, mixed-setting or malformed observations. Input timing samples must be non-boolean nonnegative integers no greater than the Rust `u128` range. Full analysis requires each `total_ns` to be positive because it is used in a logarithmic ratio; phase values may be zero. Smoke may contain zero totals and phases because it computes no ratios or confidence intervals.

For every run and each distinct row, retain baseline and candidate summaries for `total_ns` and `prepare_ns`, `instantiate_ns`, and `invoke_ns`: median, MAD, p25, p75, minimum, maximum, and p99, all with unit `ns`. Raw samples remain integer nanoseconds; interpolated summaries can be fractional nanoseconds. For `total_ns`, calculate the point estimate as `exp(median(log(candidate_total_ns / baseline_total_ns)))`, not the arithmetic median of raw ratios. Compute its deterministic 95% percentile interval by exponentiating the 2.5th and 97.5th percentiles of 10,000 resampled paired-log-ratio medians. Reuse `analyze._summary`, `analyze._bootstrap_interval`, and `analyze._seed_for`; bind the bootstrap seed to the run seed and exact row identity. Report each run independently. Never pool call counts, strategies, thresholds, rows, or the two runs. Phase summaries are descriptive only; do not bootstrap phase ratios unless separately specified by a later contract.

Do not divide by calls, calculate ns/op, infer tail latency from a batch, compute a break-even point, recommend a threshold, or issue a candidate decision. Set decision and promotion fields to null/false. Retain exact row settings (call count, strategy, threshold), raw metric name `entry_total`, raw nanosecond unit, method, confidence level, resample count, pair count, run seed, input identities and source bindings in the output.

An explicit `--allow-smoke` path is analysis-only and cannot satisfy candidate evidence. It accepts the P136 two-pair-per-row smoke only after receipt verification and source stability checks, labels `timing_evidence:false` and `gate_eligible:false`, and emits descriptive raw summaries only. Its ratio and CI fields are null. Smoke descriptives may include zero timings, but never compute logarithms or bootstrap intervals for them. Without `--allow-smoke`, refuse smoke input.

The analysis record binds the P136 report content hash and identity digest, all referenced inputs and helpers, analysis settings, and recomputable result. Verify those identities again after analysis; write only to a new exclusive output path. Re-analysis of identical inputs must produce the same statistics and record content apart from explicitly excluded creation metadata.

Validate the report through P136's collector validator; verify the complete source/build/executable/fixture/helper closure; then analyze raw totals/phases without launching Wasm. Separate full candidate-compatible evidence from smoke descriptives. Enforce the two-run complete matrix and >=30 complete pairs per row/run, positive full-analysis timings, unique row/run joins, and source/settings identity. For each run and row, summarize each side in raw ns; compute paired total ratios and a separate deterministic 10,000-resample CI. Do not calculate an aggregate across runs or policy settings.

tasks.title: Expose source-bound Register cache diagnostics
tasks.input_output_contract:
Expose `Module::register_cache_snapshot() -> Option<RegisterCacheSnapshot>` only when both `register-executor` and `execution-reference` features are enabled. A snapshot is an owned copy of numeric diagnostic fields, available on demand; it executes no guest code, mutates no cache state, clones no artifact `Arc`, and returns `None` for a poisoned cache or a foreign owner. The API and all aggregate storage are absent unless both features are enabled. Ordinary eager Register modules and default/Decoded modules return `None` for a lazy-cache snapshot.

Each snapshot identifies the owning engine, threshold, entry limit, and active body. It includes at most 64 resident entries in insertion order. Each row records body index, entry count, local preparation attempts, state (`Cold`, `Compiling`, `Ready`, `Cooldown` with remaining count, or `Negative`), and ready-artifact retained bytes. It also reports settled-ledger remaining attempted/work amounts and retained bytes/limit; active builder debits settle only when the attempt finishes, plus lifetime saturating counts for preparation starts, actual builder starts, completed preparations, published artifacts, publication failures, declined, exhausted, invalid, aborted, and evictions. `preparation_starts` counts an admitted lease even if wrapper allocation exhausts before the builder; `builder_starts` counts only an actual builder call. `completed` records `Preparation::Complete` even if owner/budget validation prevents publication; `published` counts successful Ready publication, and `publication_failures` counts completed-but-unpublished results. Snapshot code acquires cache state before the ledger, follows the established lock order, copies only scalar state while guarded, and never holds either lock while invoking guest or builder code.

Lifecycle aggregates are fixed-size scalars, saturating, and included in the existing cache metadata size accounting. Update them only at the corresponding existing lifecycle transition; never infer compile/preparation work from dispatch or invocation counters. The diagnostic build briefly updates builder-start accounting under the state lock before releasing it and calling the builder; the builder runs with both state and ledger locks released. Diagnostics must not change cache policy, retained artifact lifetime, cooldown/retry decisions, optimizer work, guest fuel, or observable semantics.

Emit a separate diagnostic JSON trace that identifies the fixture/body and records the cache states/counters without timestamps or duration fields. Each emitted trace row is explicitly `instrumented: true` and `timing_evidence: false`; its source-bound containing report additionally records `gate_eligible: false` and `candidate_promoted: false`. Traces are not input to P136/P137 timing analysis and cannot promote a candidate.

The checked-in MVP fixture exports `f00` through `f65`, each `(param i32) (result i32)` and returning the input plus its function index. Its provenance records the MIT license and WAT/Wasm hashes. The independent oracle checks each result without using the runtime's prepared artifact as expected output. Include the implicit function-end event in source-fuel accounting.

If the checkout no longer matches that commit, stop and record the actual verified predecessor in a distinct new path; never overwrite or relabel an existing archive.

Increment exactly at eviction, admitted preparation start, actual builder start, completion, successful publication or publication failure, and each settled decline, exhaustion, invalid result, or abort. tasks.title: Add individual-entry Register timing and diagnostics
tasks.input_output_contract:
Add two strict protocols: `--entry-sequence FILE INPUT SCHEDULE_THRESHOLD register eager|adaptive THRESHOLD` and `--entry-sequence-diagnostic FILE INPUT SCHEDULE_THRESHOLD register eager|adaptive THRESHOLD`. Parse and validate the entire argument vector before opening `FILE`. Require the fixed Register mode, schedule threshold `N` in `1..=64`, `eager` with engine threshold `0`, and `adaptive` with engine threshold exactly equal to schedule threshold N. Do not accept fuel, warmup, batch invocation, duplicate settings, unknown modes, non-integers, booleans-as-numbers, zero adaptive thresholds, or out-of-range schedule thresholds. Use the checked-in P138 `uniform66.wasm` bytes unchanged.

Generate a deterministic schedule that calls each export `f00` through `f65` exactly `N+1` times in order, then revisits `f00` exactly `N+1` times. Each call invokes one export once, in one Store and one module instance. Compute the independent expected result as the wrapping `i32` sum of the input and the numeric body index; check every returned result. No guest fuel is configured.

The eager side uses ordinary eager Register execution with effective entry threshold zero. The adaptive side uses P140's explicit positive threshold. Both sides receive identical fixture bytes, input, schedule threshold and call order. Separate module preparation and instantiation durations from entry observations. In `timing` mode, time each `Store::invoke` individually and only: do not include snapshot reads, result formatting, logging, command processing or I/O in `elapsed_ns`. Emit ordered raw records with `{body,visit,phase,result,elapsed_ns}`, distinguishing the initial pass from the revisit. Timing builds use `runtime-only,register-executor` without `execution-reference` or performance counters and set `instrumented:false`.

In `--entry-sequence-diagnostic` mode, require `execution-reference` and execute the identical call schedule without timers. Capture per-call P138 cache state/counters and dispatch deltas, independently validate each expected result, and verify cold, compile, ready and recompile transitions against the deterministic schedule. The Python policy assigns phase-specific cold/compile/warm/recompile classes from exact body/visit/phase positions; the diagnostic wire independently validates observed state and counter transitions. Prove the second `f00` series occurs after its FIFO eviction from the 64-entry cache. Diagnostic builds use `runtime-only,compact-executor,register-executor,execution-reference`, and their per-call wires set `instrumented:true` and `diagnostic:true` without duration or timestamp fields. The source-bound smoke report carries `timing_evidence:false`, `gate_eligible:false`, and `candidate_promoted:false`; diagnostic wires remain separate from timing observations.
implementation_steps: Confirm the completed P138 and P140 prerequisite identities and fixture provenance. Freeze the current P140 source/feature inputs for the producer contract; keep all generated outputs under a fresh, exclusive P141 target directory.

Add the new leaf module to the existing protocol dispatcher. Implement strict argument parsing and validation before file reads; share one validated schedule representation between timing and diagnostic modes. Keep the timing build uninstrumented and require `execution-reference` only for diagnostic builds.

Build eager and adaptive Register engines with the exact requested settings, compile the uniform fixture, and instantiate once. In timing mode isolate preparation and instantiation durations and time only one `Store::invoke` at a time. Keep serialization and all I/O outside every invoke timer.

Implement diagnostic observations as a separate no-timer path. Take P138 snapshots and dispatch deltas around calls; validate every result and check observed state/counter transitions against the deterministic schedule, and verify the `f00` eviction and recompile against the documented FIFO limit.

Add the three actual named Rust tests for strict parsing/build rejection, full 66-body/revisit execution, and oracle/FIFO recompile. Add four Python policy tests plus the seven existing execution-identity compatibility tests. Add producer checks for source/fixture identities, ordered records, exact counts, timer isolation, diagnostic wire shape and non-promoting smoke fields.

Preserve the actual source-bound attempt, including both feature-specific Cargo test groups, the production build, four timing observations and four diagnostic observations (2010 calls per lane), raw commands and outputs. If a checker-only fix follows collection, bind the previously passing, source-current attempt unchanged; rerun the Python policy suite and read-only producer revalidation only. Retain and identify any failed/superseded verification attempt rather than replacing it.
fixture_cases: `p141_sequence_parser_and_build_reject_before_fixture_io`: accept the exact timing and diagnostic switches; reject malformed schedules, mismatched thresholds, non-Register mode, bad strategy, duplicates, fuel and unknown options before attempting a missing fixture, and reject incompatible build features before file access.

`p141_sequence_executes_every_initial_and_revisit_entry`: run all 66 bodies through `N+1` calls and revisit `f00`; verify ordered body/visit/phase records and exact call counts for both strategies and modes.

`p141_sequence_oracle_and_fifo_recompile_are_checked`: validate every wrapping result, observed P138 lifecycle/cache state, 64-entry eviction and f00 recompile; ensure diagnostic wires contain no timing or timestamp fields.
`test_exact_schedule_and_wraparound_oracle_for_all_thresholds`: validate schedule cardinality and wrapping i32 oracle at schedule thresholds 1, 3, 10 and 64.
`test_rejects_exact_type_count_order_oracle_and_extra_field_drift`: reject wire type, ordering, count, oracle and unknown-field drift.
`test_rejects_instrumented_or_mixed_timing_and_diagnostic_wires`: reject timed/diagnostic schema mixing and instrumentation mismatches.
`test_adaptive_transition_drift_and_eager_diagnostic_contract`: reject observed cache/counter drift and invalid eager diagnostics.

tasks.evidence_contract: Bind the immutable P141-before archive/manifest, P138 and P140 prerequisite envelopes, source-current attempt-0001 freeze/verify reports and raw outputs, all three Rust case names and 11 Python policy/identity cases, production build, four timing and four diagnostic wires (2010 calls per lane), actual command logs, and final checker-only revalidation receipt. Preserve the failed verification attempt. Require final proof timing_evidence:false, gate_eligible:false, candidate_promoted:false, guest_or_build_launched:false, and decision null; make no threshold recommendation or performance claim.

diagnostic instrumentation is excluded from timing measurements
P066 retains every existing semantic, focused-stage, control, build/dependency, cold/churn, statistical, and promotion gate
tasks.title: Collect and analyze source-bound Register cold and churn sequences
tasks.input_output_contract:
Freeze the immediate P141 predecessor and complete identities for the P138 core, P141 harness/driver, uniform66 fixture, P139/P141 prerequisite proofs, and freeze helpers. Pin the predecessor commit and manifest, and require the P138 build budgets to validate and be reused because core source is unchanged. Freeze exactly two rows (`N=3`, `N=10`) and seeds `142001`, `142002`.

Retain the successful eager baseline and adaptive candidate adapter builds from verify attempt `attempt-0001`, produced with P136's isolated Register adapter machinery and the same P141 protocol/driver overlay. The final verify phase must source-current revalidate both immutable adapters, their original build commands and environment, and their separate binary/source identities without compiling or launching a guest. Measure consumes those same retained adapter directories directly; reject aliasing or drift before collection and recheck source stability afterward.

Collect exactly two complete process pairs per row over the two distinct seeds (eight pairs total). Each process is a fresh engine/module/store lifetime. Randomize eager/adaptive order deterministically within each pair. Preserve actual argv, command stdout/stderr, ordered raw per-invocation records, preparation/instantiation observations, fixture/source/binary identities, and process results. Reject missing, extra or reordered calls, body/visit/phase mismatches, bad oracle results, invalid timings, incomplete/duplicate pairs, mixed identities, and source/settings drift on resume.

The timed rows use P141's uninstrumented timing protocol. Validate the separate no-timer diagnostic traces independently and join event classes to timed records only by exact ordered `(body,visit,phase)` keys. Keep diagnostic instrumentation and its wires out of timing records. The fixed schedule exercises cold, compile, ready, FIFO eviction, and `f00` recompile behavior.

Analyze each run, row, side, and validated event class independently. Reduce each process's calls to p50, p99, and maximum before pairing; never pool calls as independent samples, combine seeds or rows, divide by calls, or mix preparation/instantiation with entry latency. Because this is a two-pair smoke, paired ratios and confidence intervals remain null and no bootstrap uncertainty is manufactured. Report `timing_evidence:false`, `gate_eligible:false`, `candidate_promoted:false`, `decision:null`, and `threshold_selection:null`. This foundation smoke cannot satisfy the full P066 cold/churn evidence requirement.
implementation_steps: Validate the completed P139/P141 prerequisite envelopes and P138 fixture provenance. Freeze the exact P142 predecessor, rows and source identities before building.

Revalidate the successful P136-based baseline and current-candidate adapters retained from verify attempt `attempt-0001`; preserve their distinct source and executable identities and common P141 overlay without rebuilding during final verification.
Run the collector with two seeds and two process pairs per row. Keep raw commands, outputs and checkpoint records; validate all retained pairs and source identities before resuming.
Validate the separate P141 diagnostic class map and exact call-key join; keep instrumented diagnostic records separate from timed observations.
Run the descriptive analyzer on the source-bound smoke. Retain per-process event summaries and null inferential fields without manufacturing confidence intervals or a decision.
Verify with focused collector, identity and analyzer tests. Use only temporary synthetic fixtures in tests and ensure every test output remains within its fresh temporary root.

Close the task with the two-pair smoke explicitly marked non-timing and nonpromoting. Preserve all phase receipts and raw logs; do not claim a threshold recommendation, performance result, or P066 gate completion.
fixture_cases: `test_smoke_collects_contained_source_bound_pairs_and_replays`: collect and replay the fixed two-row, two-seed, two-pair smoke while rejecting paths outside the safe collection root.
`test_failure_preserves_first_side_and_resume_uses_new_attempts`: retain the first side after failure and resume only with new attempts after validating checkpoint and identities.
`test_report_rejects_wire_order_and_raw_record_corruption`: reject reordered event records and mutation of retained raw wire data.
`test_rows_runs_classes_and_ci_are_separate_and_deterministic`: preserve run/row/event-class separation and stable descriptive analysis.
`test_smoke_requires_opt_in_and_has_descriptive_null_uncertainty`: require explicit smoke analysis opt-in and keep inferential values null.
`test_bad_sample_count_payload_shape_and_stale_fixture_are_rejected`: reject bad sample shapes, changed fixtures, and invalid smoke counts.
`test_analysis_changes_are_visible_but_do_not_stale_legacy_pairs`: ensure source identities capture the intended analysis boundary without invalidating unrelated legacy pairs.
`test_adapter_archive_corruption_is_still_rejected`: reject corrupted predecessor adapter archives.
